name: Hoshea, last king of Israel
charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord, though not as the kings before him; conspiring with So king of Egypt and withholding the tribute
summary: Hoshea the son of Elah, the last king of Israel, did evil though not as the kings before him; he became Shalmaneser’s servant and paid him tribute, then sent to So king of Egypt and stopped the payments (2 Kings 17:1-4). The king of Assyria bound him in prison, besieged Samaria three years, took it in Hoshea’s ninth year, and carried Israel away to Halah, to Habor by the river of Gozan, and to the cities of the Medes (2 Kings 17:4-6). It came because they would not obey the voice of the Lord their God (2 Kings 18:12).
offenseFull: Pekah had killed Pekahiah and lost half the land to Assyria, and Hoshea conspired against Pekah and killed him the same way (2 Kings 15:25, 29-30); what a man sows he reaps (Galatians 6:7). In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea began to reign in Samaria nine years, about 732 to 722 BC in the teaching, and did evil in the sight of the Lord, though not as the kings of Israel before him (2 Kings 17:1-2). Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant and paid tribute (2 Kings 17:3); he was a puppet king. The splitting of the kingdom was one thing and the cutting off was another: the north still had a kingdom until 722 BC, and that is when the northern kingdom became Gentiles.

Then the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and brought no tribute as he had year by year (2 Kings 17:4). He turned to Egypt, the first nation that enslaved them, instead of to the Lord. Ephraim was like a silly dove without sense, calling to Egypt and going to Assyria (Hosea 7:11), and the teaching reads king Jareb as no person but the great king, Shalmaneser (Hosea 5:13; Hosea 10:6). Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and trust in its shadow instead of looking to the Holy One of Israel (Isaiah 30:1-3; Isaiah 31:1). The teacher applies it to trusting in America’s politics, and Zedekiah later repeated the same pattern.
judgmentFull: The king of Assyria shut Hoshea up and bound him in prison, came up through all the land, and besieged Samaria three years; in Hoshea’s ninth year he took Samaria, carried Israel away to Assyria, and placed them in Halah and Habor by the river of Gozan and in the cities of the Medes (2 Kings 17:4-6; 2 Kings 18:9-11). A siege meant the famine the law had warned of, until they ate the fruit of their own bodies (Deuteronomy 28:52-53). This Shalmaneser is the Enemessar of Tobit, who carried Tobit of Naphtali to Nineveh (Tobit 1:2). The captives were led away with hooks (Amos 4:2) along a long road through Damascus and Hamath, across the Euphrates to the Habor and Media, which is why northern Israelites turn up later in Corinth, Galatia and Macedonia. The captivity came in waves: Tiglath-pileser had already taken Galilee and Naphtali (2 Kings 15:29), and a remnant stayed in the land, the ones Hezekiah called to his Passover (2 Chronicles 30:6).

It came because they did not obey the voice of the Lord their God but broke His covenant and all that Moses commanded, and would neither hear it nor do it (2 Kings 18:12). That is what Amos was telling them was going to happen; they did not want to hear it, and it happened (2 Kings 17:23). The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath and Sepharvaim and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the children of Israel (2 Kings 17:24). Yet the Lord would sift the house of Israel among all nations like grain in a sieve, and not the least kernel would fall to the ground (Amos 9:9). Because of the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob He will always bring them back, for there cannot be twelve tribes if ten of them are missing.

text.text: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him.
Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents.

And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison.

And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
Because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord their God, but transgressed his covenant, and all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded, and would not hear them, nor do them.

But Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him, and smote him in Samaria, in the palace of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh, and with him fifty men of the Gileadites: and he killed him, and reigned in his room.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel–beth–maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.
And Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and smote him, and slew him, and reigned in his stead, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years.
And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him.
Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and gave him presents.

And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison.
Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah saw his wound, then went Ephraim to the Assyrian, and sent to king Jareb: yet could he not heal you, nor cure you of your wound.
It shall be also carried unto Assyria for a present to king Jareb: Ephraim shall receive shame, and Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel.
Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin:
That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!
Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion.

Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!
And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria, and besieged it.
And at the end of three years they took it: even in the sixth year of Hezekiah, that is the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.
And the king of Assyria did carry away Israel unto Assyria, and put them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes:

And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land: and he shall besiege thee in all thy gates throughout all thy land, which the Lord thy God hath given thee.

And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee:
Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians was led captive out of Thisbe, which is at the right hand of that city, which is called properly Nephthali in Galilee above Aser.
The Lord God hath sworn by his holiness, that, lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel–beth–maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.

So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Israel and Judah, and according to the commandment of the king, saying, Ye children of Israel, turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.
Until the Lord removed Israel out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Israel carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.

And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel: and they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof.
For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.
